as_told.title: Encyclopedia diagram of Pioneer 10 showing a dead star

plain: This story is about Pioneer 10 and 11, two space probes sent toward the outer solar system. A researcher, Matt LaCroix, says that an encyclopedia from 1987, called the New Science Encyclopedia, has a diagram of what the probes found. According to him, it shows that scientists at the time thought there was an object about 50 billion miles away, which he describes as a dead companion star, and he credits Thomas Van Flandern and Robert Harrington. He comes back to it several times in the same podcast episode. At one point he dates the encyclopedia to 1983 instead and points to a label on the diagram reading equal gravitational pull. If true, it would mean a large hidden body in our solar system was once quietly noted and then forgotten.
